quotes.text: In the Dashboard, make sure you’ve added domains to the [domain allowlist](https://dashboard.stripe.com/crypto-onramp/allowlist-domains) for the domains you’ll use to host the onramp page.
An `OnrampSession` object tracks the customer’s onramp lifecycle, keeping track of order details and ensuring the customer is only charged once.
Our official libraries don’t contain built-in support for the API endpoints because the onramp API is in limited beta.

These scripts must always load directly from Stripe’s domains (https://js.stripe.com and https://crypto-js.stripe.com) for compatibility. Don’t include the scripts in a bundle or host a copy yourself.

old_evidence.text: Add an endpoint on your server that creates an OnrampSession object. An OnrampSession object tracks the customer's onramp lifecycle, keeping track of order details and ensuring the customer is only charged once.
Our official libraries don't contain built-in support for the API endpoints because the onramp API is in limited beta.
Call `loadStripeOnramp()` with your Stripe publishable API key to configure the Stripe library.
`onramp_session_updated` — fires on any session status change (`onChange` prop)

findings: The November same-URL capture keeps the test-key embedded onramp purpose, domain allowlist, server-created OnrampSession/client-secret handoff, React loadStripeOnramp and mounted iframe, callbacks, and sandbox context (old 4-96, 98-233; new 5-9, 171-305, 848-902). The new 940-line capture also flattens many language/framework code panels and setup commands into one text stream (new 11-170, 306-845); these adjacent snippets are alternatives, not one runnable program or a demonstrated successful purchase.

The new capture adds server examples in Ruby, Python, PHP, Go, .NET and Java alongside Node and a separate direct browser-script path (new 37-170, 306-338, 702-845, 866-900). The old capture is specifically Node/React (old 8-96). The existing source summary line 13 remains accurate for its May raw but should be dated and expanded to acknowledge the November variants without blending incompatible examples.

For the direct script path, the November guide explicitly says load Stripe.js and crypto-js scripts from Stripe domains rather than bundling or self-hosting (new 866-872). The existing source only describes the React package path (source 27-39); keep the browser-script qualification scoped to the script variant, not an invented ban on installing the React packages.

Both captures retain limited-beta and custom-extension prose (old 18-22; new 848-852). However the new Java sample invokes client.v1().crypto().onrampSessions().create(params) and a .NET OnrampSessionService (new 139-170), which conflicts with an unqualified assertion that no official library has built-in endpoint support. The source line 17 and concept's Embedded Integration section should preserve the older Node custom-extension example as dated, narrow the broad library claim, and record the new-page internal tension rather than infer general availability.

Existing source line 25 and concept's Embedded Integration section call destination_currency, destination_exchange_amount, destination_network and customer_ip_address 'required'. Both captures show these fields passed in a server example (old 43-57; new 24-36), but neither supplies a complete request schema proving universal requiredness. Reword as the sample's sent fields. The browser submits transaction_details; the server obtains the IP separately, so the wording must preserve client/server identity.

The source's callbacks and sample transaction values remain example-specific (old 117-146, 227-229, 287-289; new 178-209, 299-304). Session status updates are not evidence of payment finality or delivered crypto. The page states the session object is intended to avoid charging a customer twice (new 848-850) but shows no executed transaction, webhook receipt, settlement, or bank result.
substantive_changes: More explicit multi-language and direct browser-script integration variants are included in the November capture, while the older capture is Node/React (old 8-96; new 11-170, 306-338, 702-845, 866-900).
The November direct-script instructions explicitly require Stripe-hosted script loading for compatibility (new 866-868); this instruction is absent from the May Node/React quickstart.
A new Java sample uses a client.v1().crypto().onrampSessions().create call, creating tension with the guide's unchanged blanket limited-beta library note (new 165-166, 852).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 2026 Node/React path and its custom StripeResource extension as historical example code (old 18-62, 98-233); do not interpret extra November variants as removal of the prior path.
Preserve limited-beta wording as captured, qualified to the page/date and reconciled with newer variant snippets before broad SDK claims (old 22; new 852, 139-170).

Preserve the server/client boundary: the server uses a secret key to create the session and returns clientSecret; the browser uses a publishable key and clientSecret to mount the iframe (old 24-57, 98-146; new 14-36, 171-209).
Preserve the domain allowlist and test-key/sandbox framing, and do not infer live eligibility or completed crypto delivery (old 4-6, 96; new 9, 896-902).
conflicts: New raw 852 states no official library has built-in support, while new Java example 165-166 calls client.v1().crypto().onrampSessions().create(params) and .NET example 139-146 uses OnrampSessionService. This same-page inconsistency does not establish SDK release status; source line 17 and the concept must not universalize the older Node custom-extension note.
Source line 25 and concept's Embedded Integration section assert sample fields are required, but old 43-57 and new 24-36 are examples rather than request-schema evidence.

The new flattened capture juxtaposes alternative code fragments, including two fetch endpoint strings in the same displayed call (new 179-197, 312-327), so it cannot be treated as one executable integration without selecting a particular variant.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not establish which official SDK versions support the onramp endpoint, whether the Java/.NET examples are directly executable, or whether limited-beta access is available to this merchant.
No onramp session was created or paid in this review; the document's lifecycle description cannot prove a charge, final crypto delivery, or a bank receipt.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-quickstart, the November capture expands the May Node/React sample into multiple server and browser variants (old lines 8-96; new lines 11-170 and 306-338). It still describes a server-created OnrampSession and browser client-secret handoff (old lines 18-22; new lines 848-852). [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-quickstart]] should date its Node/React evidence and distinguish the newly captured alternatives, including the direct Stripe-hosted script rule at new lines 866-868.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-quickstart, [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-quickstart]] should qualify two broad claims: fields shown in old lines 43-57 and new lines 24-36 are sample inputs, not a proved universal required schema; and the old custom-library warning at line 22 remains in new line 852 despite a new Java client method at lines 165-166. The capture proves neither general SDK support nor merchant eligibility or payment completion.
